title: selinum carvi
intro: Selinum carvi, commonly known as Caraway, is a biennial herb native to Europe and Asia, belonging to the carrot family (Apiaceae). It is valued for its seeds, which have been used in traditional medicine for their health benefits, including relieving digestive issues, reducing inflammation, and acting as a mild sedative. The therapeutic actions of Caraway seeds include carminative, anti-inflammatory, and antispasmodic properties, which make them effective in treating symptoms such as bloating, cramps, and fever. The bioactive constituents of Caraway seeds include carvone, limonene, and fenchone, which contribute to their medicinal properties.
